assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes (confidence high)
daemon_capability: full, for the generic failure->error mechanism only -- see "The central open question" below
driver_capability: ready (base_url_override already wired by sibling cell 2-14, no new driver work needed)
route: record

This cell was flagged by the dispatcher as one of exactly two muse traits (with `burndown_progression`) that prior capability research could find NO EVIDENCE EITHER WAY for -- left undeclared rather than marked absent. This assessment does NOT lean into either answer without evidence; it reports what a deep binary-string + wire-schema + code + live-`--help` investigation actually found, and is explicit about what remains unresolved. No real or mocked quota exhaustion was induced -- inducing a real one would burn the maintainer's account; inducing an authentically quota-shaped MOCKED one is blocked on not knowing Meta's undocumented backend wire protocol (see below). Every claim below cites what was run or read.

## agent_supports = yes -- muse has a real, product-level quota/subscription-exhaustion feature

`strings` on the real installed binary (`/Users/ingo/.local/bin/muse-bin-1.2.1-R2847.1`, 273MB, muse-stable channel) surfaces, verbatim:

- A slash-command help table (one contiguous string blob) listing `/usage` ("Show session usage"), `/cost` (immediately adjacent, no separate description text -> reads as an alias sharing /usage's behavior, matching the task brief's "/usage exists as a real command (aliases /cost, /context)"), and `/upgrade` ("Show your subscription plan") as real, distinct slash commands alongside `/status`, `/permissions`, `/tasks`.
- A short TUI-banner-id cluster: `quota_hit`, `spend_nudge`, `resume`, sitting directly after the slash-command table.
- A PLAIN-TEXT documentation/migration-note string (not code, reads like an embedded doc comment) that names the mechanism explicitly: "...the /upgrade command, the upsell surfaces (login_flow, spend_nudge, payment_banner), and the quota-hit failure entry's upgrade arm (quota_hit, QH-FR-006); the retired /subscription command's subscription_command value appears only in pre-consolidation records." This confirms: a formal "quota-hit failure entry" concept exists, cross-referenced to an internal ticket id, with a dedicated "upgrade arm"; a `/subscription` command existed historically and was consolidated/retired.
- An internal field name `quota_hit_out` sitting inside a large pool of session-runtime "pending work" field names (`pending_hook_records`, `notification_hook_tasks`, `workflow_launcher`, `quota_hit_out`, `goal_revision_guard`, ...) -- reads as an outbound-notification-queue field on the session runtime struct.
- A clean PascalCase identifier `QuotaHit` (Rust source variant-name casing) recovered from a second, unrelated code region (TIFF/image tag string pool) -- independent corroboration this is a genuine internal enum discriminant, not an artifact of string-concatenation noise (the string pool has no delimiters between adjacent constants, so a single low-confidence hit could be coincidental; two independent occurrences in unrelated code regions is not).
- A separate, clean PascalCase identifier `PaymentSubscriptionRequired`, found in a provider/credential-construction error cluster (alongside `ModelProviderConstructionError`, `NoDefaultModel`, `NoExplicitProviderModel`, `UnsupportedProviderOption`, `CredentialRejected`, `AuthRequired`) -- an internal error variant distinct from the wire's public `TurnErrorKind`/`ErrorKind` (neither string appears anywhere in the 224KB extracted `msp.schema.json`), most plausibly fired at session/model-start time when a paid tier gate blocks provider selection.
- A fully-formed internal telemetry model: `SubscriptionUsageSnapshot { window: SubscriptionWindowSnapshot { used_percent, window_duration_mins, resets_at }, weekly: SubscriptionWeeklySnapshot { used_percent, resets_at, window_duration_mins }, tier }`, plus an event-shaped name `SubscriptionUsageReceived { received_at, ... }`. `resets_at` is exactly the "budget resets" concept the scenario's acceptance criteria names.

Combined, this settles the ambiguity: muse clearly implements quota/subscription-exhaustion handling as a first-class product feature (upsell UI, a named failure-entry class, usage telemetry with reset timestamps), not merely a theoretical provider-side possibility.

## daemon_capability = full, but only for the mechanism -- NOT confirmed for the quota-specific signal

### What IS proven (cites live, executed evidence)

Muse's `--help` (run live on this machine, muse-bin 1.2.1-R2847.1) documents `--base-url <URL>` ("Override the Meta provider base URL") as a deterministic way to force every model call in a run to fail with zero API cost -- point it at a dead local port. Sibling cell `replaydata/agents/muse/scenarios/2-14_turn-aborted-by-error` used exactly this mechanism and, after three live recording attempts (the first two blocked by an unrelated daemon PID-eviction bug, fixed by commit 9abf13d1), LIVE-CONFIRMED: a run whose model call fails produces `event.kind:"terminal","terminal":"failed"` with a free-text `reason` (captured live: `"transport error: error sending request for url (http://127.0.0.1:18799/responses) (after 4 provider attempts)"` -- note the `/responses` path, see below), which `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`'s `parseRunTerminal` (~line 317-365) turns into `ev.SessionError{Phase:ErrorPhaseUnknown, Class:<error_class or "terminal_failed">, Message:<reason>}`. `core/application/services/state_classifier.go`'s `session_error` rule (~line 283-289, `id: string(session.SignalSessionError)`) fires whenever `SessionError != nil && !HookTurnDone` and decides `session.StateError` directly; muse declares no hooks (`agent.go`: "observe-only ... no hooks"), so `HookTurnDone` is always false and this rule fires unconditionally. `classifyAgentDone` (~line 396-452) independently converges on the same `StateError` outcome as a second path. 2-14's third live attempt (recording `2026-09-14-06-40-20_irrlichd-0.6.3+9abf13d`) confirmed the resulting arc cleanly: `ready -> working -> error`, sticky (no reversion to `waiting`/`ready` for the rest of the session's life -- `SessionError` clears only on the user's next fresh turn, per `clearSessionErrorOnRecovery`).

Per Irrlicht's own `StateError` doc (`core/domain/session/session.go`): "the provider refused or failed the call ... It exists so such a session is visibly red instead of silently green." A quota/budget rejection IS "the provider refused the call" by this definition. Sibling scenarios `claudecode/2-23_provider-overloaded-terminal` and `claudecode/2-24_auth-credentials-rejected` (checked directly) both assert exactly `ready->working->error`, `Final state: error` for the architecturally identical event class (a provider call fails, the agent gives up) -- direct, repo-internal precedent that this is the matrix's recognized, intentional pattern for a provider-refusal class event, not a defect. The scenario 2-9's own literal wording ("Final state: ready") was written against claudecode's OLDER behavior (see "claudecode's own cell may be stale" below) and does not fit muse's architecture, for the same reason 2-14 already documented for muse in detail (muse has no "silent recovery" code path anywhere in the 14+2-session corpus or the format-spec research -- every captured failure produced a `terminal` event of some kind).

### The central open question -- NOT resolved by this assessment

Whether an actual quota/budget rejection is DISTINGUISHABLE, in the daemon's observed trace, from any other model-call failure (config error, idle timeout, dead-port connection refusal) is UNVERIFIED:

- No wire-schema vocabulary exists for it: the documented `ErrorKind` (37 values) and `TurnErrorKind` (9 values, `stepLimit|configError|projectionError|logError|workflowLaunchError|environmentError|modelError|launchError|authRequired`) enums -- both fully enumerated by reading `msp.schema.json` directly -- contain no `quota`/`rateLimit`/`usageLimit`/`subscriptionLimit`-shaped value. The `PaymentSubscriptionRequired`/`SubscriptionUsageSnapshot` vocabulary found in the binary does not appear anywhere in the 224KB extracted wire schema (`account/read`'s result, `AccountState`, is a closed 3-field shape: `credentialRequired`, `label`, `state` -- no usage/percent/reset field at all). The one wire notification that DOES carry a free-text `reason` mid-turn, `turn/retryScheduled` ("attempt N/M - retrying in Ss - reason"), folds from a `kind:"task"` durable record the muse adapter's parser currently skips entirely (`ev.Skip=true`, package doc's default branch) -- so even if a real quota-triggered retry-then-give-up sequence exists, nothing reads it today.
- The exhaustive corpus text scan (format-spec.md SS11, my own re-verification via the same method) found zero occurrences of `quota`/`rate_limit`/`overloaded`/`subscription`/`compact`/`context_limit` as a literal anywhere in the 14+2 available real sessions. The one genuine failure example on record is `reason:"model stream idle timeout after 30000ms"` -- a stream-level timeout, not a quota/limit message.
- `--base-url` only overrides "the Meta provider base URL" (its own `--help` text) -- it redirects the SAME Meta-internal wire protocol to an alternate host; it is NOT a generic "speak any provider's API" switch. The 2-14 live capture's `reason` text names a `/responses`-shaped path, suggesting Meta's backend proxy is OpenAI-Responses-API-like rather than Anthropic-Messages-API-like, but this is inferred from one URL fragment, not confirmed against any request/response schema. Building a mock server that returns an AUTHENTIC quota-rejection response (as opposed to a bare dead-port connection refusal) requires knowing that undocumented wire shape -- something this assessment could not establish and did not attempt to guess. Fabricating one would be exactly the "decode unlabeled protobuf with no ground truth" anti-pattern this skill's push-through guidance warns against.
- Separately, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL`/`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`/`OPENROUTER_BASE_URL`/`MUSE_MODEL` env-var NAMES exist in the binary's string table, adjacent to `TBH_EVAL_APPEND_SYSTEM_PROMPT`/`TBH_IS_E2E_TEST` (an internal eval-harness cluster) and to `MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER_TOOL_SWITCH` (one of ~45 `MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_*` feature-gate names also found). Live `muse --help`/`muse auth set --help`/`muse login --help` show the PUBLIC surface does NOT expose these: `--provider` accepts only `echo|meta`, `muse auth set --provider` accepts only `meta`, and `login`'s own help text says "META_API_KEY always takes priority over the account login." So whether these env vars actually reroute live model traffic (which would let `record` reuse claudecode's exact mock-Anthropic-429 pattern safely) or are dead/eval-only code is UNCONFIRMED. This is a promising lead for `record` to test cheaply and safely (worst case: the env vars are ignored and muse falls back to needing a real Meta credential, which `record` would notice immediately without ever sending a request) but is not a proven mechanism.

### Consequence for what can honestly be recorded

The SAFE, PROVEN mechanism (`--base-url` at a dead port, exactly 2-14's recipe) would produce a recording that is daemon-trace-IDENTICAL to 2-14's own fixture -- same `ready->working->error` arc, same `session_error` classifier rule, likely the same generic "transport error" reason text. Recorded as-is, this cell would NOT exercise anything quota-specific and would silently duplicate 2-14 -- precisely the vacuous-pass shape this skill's own worked example (copilot 2-11 duplicating 2-2) warns about. Two ways `record` could genuinely improve on this, in descending order of authenticity: (1) confirm whether the `MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_PROVIDER_TOOL_SWITCH`-adjacent env vars actually reroute model calls, and if so build a minimal stateful stub (succeed once, 429 the second call) mirroring `tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-anthropic-429`; (2) failing that, at minimum have the dead-port stub return a bare HTTP 429 status (not a raw connection refusal) at the `/responses` path, and record whatever `reason`/`error_class` text muse's client produces for THAT case, checking whether it differs meaningfully from the connection-refused case -- even an unstructured "rate limited"-flavored string would be a strictly stronger, if still unverified, signal than reusing 2-14 unmodified. If neither yields a distinguishing signal, `record` should say so plainly rather than recording a near-duplicate under this scenario's name.

### claudecode's own 2-9 cell may be stale, for the same reason

`replaydata/agents/claudecode/scenarios/2-9_token-quota-exhausted/metadata.json` (recorded 2026-05-18, daemon 0.4.5) asserts "irrlicht's parser treats all turn-failure shapes as 'turn ended abnormally -> ready'" and daemon=full for a `ready` final state. `core/adapters/inbound/agents/claudecode/parser.go`/`sessionerror.go` (checked directly) now ALSO emit `SessionError` for an API error, and `core/application/services/state_classifier.go`'s `session_error` rule routes it to `StateError` the same way it does for muse -- this machinery (issue #1798/#1799/#1800) postdates claudecode's 2-9 recording. Whether claudecode's CURRENT daemon behavior for this exact scenario still lands in `ready` (e.g. because its Stop hook fires before SessionError is set, clearing it) or now also lands in `error` was NOT re-verified here (out of scope -- this is a muse assessment) -- flagging it because it bears directly on whether 2-9's canonical "Final state: ready" wording is still accurate for ANY hook-driven adapter with `SessionError` support, not just muse. Worth a maintainer look, not a claim of a confirmed defect.

## driver_capability = ready

No new driver work is needed: `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` already reads `settings.base_url` out of `$SETTINGS_PATH` and appends `--base-url "$value"` to the muse launch invocation (`grep` confirms lines ~100-114, ~277) -- this was ported by 2-14's `record` phase (`driver_capability` corrected `gap:base_url_override -> ready` there) and is now committed, general-purpose machinery this cell reuses as-is. `DRIVE_ELICITS` already covers every step type the recipe needs (`send`/`wait_turn`/`sleep`/`exit_clean`; `turn-count.sh`'s `turn_count()` matches any `event.kind=="terminal"` regardless of the `terminal` field's value, so it correctly unblocks on a failed run too).
caveats: Vacuous-pass check (the load-bearing one): as currently achievable with the PROVEN driver mechanism (--base-url at a dead port), this cell's recording would be daemon-trace-identical to muse/2-14_turn-aborted-by-error -- it would pass while proving nothing quota-specific. See "Consequence for what can honestly be recorded" in the body for the two concrete ways `record` could improve on this, and the fallback of saying so plainly if neither works.

No live quota exhaustion -- real (which would burn the maintainer's account) or mocked (which is blocked on not knowing Meta's undocumented backend wire protocol) -- was induced during this assessment. Every daemon-side claim about the terminal:failed->error mechanism is grounded in sibling cell 2-14's own live-recorded evidence, not a fresh live test run here.

Whether the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/OPENAI_*/OPENROUTER_* env vars found in the binary's string table actually reroute live model traffic is UNCONFIRMED -- `muse --help`/`muse auth set --help` only document `--provider echo|meta`. `record` should test this cheaply (it either works safely, or the env vars are silently ignored and nothing is sent) before relying on it.

The wire schema's session/tokenUsage and session/contextUsage notifications are confirmed (independently, by directly reading msp.schema.json's method list and property definitions) to have NO durable session.jsonl counterpart search hit and no corpus example -- consistent with the shared context's existing note that both are wire-only. No THIRD notification (e.g. session/subscriptionUsage or account/usageChanged) exists for quota/subscription usage at all -- confirmed by enumerating every session/*, account/*, turn/*, subagent/* method name in the schema directly, not by a substring search alone.

The turn/retryScheduled notification (folds from a kind:"task" durable record) carries a free-text, non-enum reason field and is observable BEFORE a turn terminates -- a plausible future signal for an automatic-retry-then-give-up quota shape -- but the muse adapter's parser currently Skip=true's every kind:"task" event by default, so nothing reads it today even if muse does emit one. Not asserted in the spec below since no corpus or live example of it exists to confirm the shape.

claudecode's own 2-9 cell (daemon 0.4.5, pre-#1798) may itself be stale now that claudecode's adapter also emits SessionError -- see body. Not verified here; flagged for the maintainer, not claimed as a confirmed defect.

cost_nonzero/tokens_nonzero asserted false, mirroring 2-14: the induced failure (dead-port connection refusal) fails before any model_completed event, so no usage is ever recorded for that turn. If record substitutes a stub that returns a real (if minimal) response body before failing, this may need reconsideration.

Session-birth shape (single birth vs. a transient proc-<PID> presession) inherits the same open question 2-13/2-14 already flag (wiring.go's unconditional per-adapter process scanner) -- phases below are written the same defensively-anchored way for consistency.

preconditions: muse CLI installed and on PATH, v1.2.1 (muse --version >= 1.2.1)
muse auth complete (muse login, or META_API_KEY exported) -- same out-of-band precondition as muse/2-1_basic-turn and muse/2-14_turn-aborted-by-error
tmux available -- the interactive driver runs muse in a tmux REPL
irrlichd is recording (either run-cell.sh isolated mode, or --attach against a running daemon started with --record)
go on PATH -- run-cell.sh's start_recipe_mock builds .mock.package with `go build` before launching it
port 18803 free on 127.0.0.1 at record time -- distinct from 2-14's dead port 18799, 2-23's mock port 18802, and 2-22's mock port 18801, so no two sibling cells can ever collide
setup: RECORD-TIME CHANGE from the assessed baseline: the assessment's own 'PREFERRED IF FEASIBLE' option (a minimal local HTTP stub at /responses returning 429, over the dead-port baseline that is daemon-trace-identical to 2-14) is what record used, per the batch brief (#1960 record pass): tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-muse-overload with --status 429 --succeed-after 0 (never succeed) -- the same mock 2-22/2-23 use, sharing infrastructure rather than inventing a quota-specific stub (no wire vocabulary for quota exists to build one authentically -- see metadata.json's 'central open question').
Same launch shape as muse/2-14_turn-aborted-by-error: a fresh empty cwd, `muse --trust-workspace --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18803` in a tmux session, 1s settle sleep before the first send.

record does NOT need to start the mock by hand: the recipe's .mock block below is read by run-cell.sh's start_recipe_mock, which builds, launches on 127.0.0.1:18803, waits for LISTEN, and tears it down in the EXIT trap.
The prompt content does not matter for cue-avoidance: the model call fails before any assistant text is generated. Keep it simple, e.g. "Say hello."

record MUST record, in this cell's own notes, whether the resulting reason/error_class text carries any quota/rate-limit-flavored content or is generic -- this is the cell's own stated acceptance question, not optional.

TIMING, carried forward from the 2-23 sibling's live drive (same mock mechanism, --status 429 --succeed-after 0): against a real HTTP 429, muse's retry ladder backs off exponentially (1s,2s,4s,8s,16s,32s, capped at 60s, across max_attempts=10) rather than near-instantly like a dead port -- ~243s of cumulative backoff before the terminal give-up. timeout_seconds set to 330 from the start to avoid re-running into the same timeout 2-23's first attempt hit.
verify: events.jsonl mints a session in ready shortly after muse's TUI finishing launching
events.jsonl contains a pid_discovered event binding the muse-bin PID to the real session
events.jsonl contains a state_transition to working when the user prompt lands
events.jsonl contains a state_transition to error after the model call fails (session_error classifier rule)
the session does NOT stick in working, and does NOT re-enter ready or waiting after the failure (error is sticky)
observation vector: tokens_nonzero=false, cost_nonzero=false (no model_completed event before the failure), model unpinned

the mock's own request log (mock.log) contains at least 1 line matching the recipe's request_log_pattern, proving muse actually reached it rather than the recording having silently fallen through to the real Meta endpoint

record must record, in the cell's own notes, whether the induced failure's reason/error_class text carries ANY quota/rate-limit-flavored content, or is generic -- this determines whether the recording meaningfully tests THIS scenario or is a documented near-duplicate of 2-23/2-14
